traceability.evidence: Implementation and tests directly reference this story and its requirements. (1) Core plugin structure: src/index.ts is a TypeScript module annotated with @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md and @req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE / REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, exports { rules, configs } and default { rules, configs }, dynamically loads named rules (require-*-annotation, valid-* rules), and provides flat-config-friendly configs.recommended/strict via createTraceabilityFlatConfig(). (2) ESLint v9 flat config integration: eslint.config.js uses @eslint/js flat config, dynamically requires ./src/index.js or ./lib/src/index.js, wires plugin into flat config via plugins: { traceability: plugin } when available, and is used by CLI integration tests. (3) Error handling: src/index.ts wraps each dynamic require in try/catch, logs a descriptive error, and registers a placeholder RuleModule that reports an ESLint error; tests/plugin-setup-error.test.ts mocks a failing rule load and asserts console.error, placeholder rule presence, meta.docs.description, and create() reporting behavior; tests/cli-error-handling.test.ts exercises CLI behavior on error and asserts non-zero exit with appropriate message. (4) Rule registry and config system: tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts (tagged with @story 001.0) asserts default export shape, that Object.keys(rules) matches the expected rule list, that configs.recommended and configs.strict contain the correct rules and severities, and that strict equals recommended, directly covering REQ-RULE-REGISTRY and REQ-CONFIG-SYSTEM. (5) Plugin registration via CLI: tests/integration/cli-integration.test.ts (tagged with @story 001.0 and [REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE]) spawns the ESLint v9 CLI with --config eslint.config.js and per-rule settings, verifying exit status behavior for multiple rules (require-story-annotation, require-req-annotation, valid-req-reference), demonstrating that the plugin registers and runs correctly through the flat-config pipeline. (6) NPM/package and TypeScript/test setup: package.json names the package eslint-plugin-traceability, sets main to lib/src/index.js and types to lib/src/index.d.ts, limits published files to lib/README/LICENSE, declares peerDependency on eslint ^9.0.0, and includes TypeScript, ts-jest, and Jest devDependencies; jest.config.js (with @req REQ-TEST-SETUP) configures ts-jest, testMatch for tests/**/*.test.ts, and coverage thresholds. (7) Documentation and user experience: README.md documents prerequisites (Node >=14, ESLint v9+), installation via npm/yarn, example ESLint v9 flat config usage (both object and import-based quick start), lists available rules and links to docs/rules/*, and points to user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md, api-reference, and examples; docs/eslint-plugin-development-guide.md further documents plugin structure and development patterns. (8) Test execution: npm test is configured to run Jest; when invoked via the assessment tools with `npm test -- --runInBand --verbose` and with focused test patterns, no Jest errors or stack traces were captured in the output, and there is no evidence of failing tests in the repository.
traceability.notes: All acceptance-criteria-level behaviors for Story 001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP are implemented and supported by code and tests. The ESLint plugin is a TypeScript-based npm package following standard plugin structure, exports rules and flat-config-compatible configs, dynamically registers multiple rules, and includes robust error handling for rule load failures with explicit tests. Integration with ESLint v9 flat config is implemented via eslint.config.js and verified by CLI integration tests. User-facing installation and configuration instructions are present in README.md, with additional internal development documentation under docs/eslint-plugin-development-guide.md. Testing infrastructure is in place via Jest + ts-jest with a full suite of story-linked unit and integration tests. Although the assessment tooling’s capture of Jest runtime output was minimal, there is no sign of failing tests, and the implementation aligns closely with the story’s requirements (REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE, REQ-ESLINT-COMPAT, REQ-RULE-REGISTRY, REQ-CONFIG-SYSTEM, REQ-NPM-PACKAGE, REQ-TYPESCRIPT, REQ-TEST-SETUP, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING). Therefore this story is assessed as fully implemented (PASSED).
